title: fix(console,app-shell,auth): one request per resource on console open — entitlements, get-session, runtime/config (objectui#12808)
body:
Fixes #12808
Clause-②: yes

Each of the three resources the card measured is now fetched once per console open.

## What changed, per resource

**Environment entitlements** (`packages/app-shell/src/environment/useEnvironmentEntitlements.ts`). Every reader of `useEnvironmentEntitlements` now shares one resource per control-plane origin and organisation. The resource holds the in-flight resolution and the settled answer (the summary, with the row-derived fallback when the summary is unavailable). The readers are the three `cloud:plan-status` cards, `cloud:onboarding-next`, `cloud:workspace-timezone-notice` and the environment list. `CloudOnboardingNext` drops its own fetch and reads the shared resource; only a `summary` answer resolves it, so a failed or row-derived answer still reads as `unknown`, as before. The resource is refetched when the organisation changes, and when a reader's `refreshKey` moves: the environment list after a create explicitly re-resolves the shared answer, and every reader gets the new one. Nothing is time-based. The answer lives only while at least one reader is mounted. The drop waits for the end of the current task, so an unmount and a mount committed together hand the answer over. A later mount asks the server again, as every mount did before.

**Session** (`apps/console/src/lib/auth-preflight.ts`, `packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts`, `packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx`). When the preflight finds the stored Bearer valid, it leaves its `get-session` answer in a page-load slot on `globalThis` (`Symbol.for('objectui.authPreflightSession')`) along with the auth URL and the token it asked with. `AuthProvider` takes the answer once, in a `useState` initializer, as its first state, and its mount effect does not ask again. That includes the StrictMode effect replay. The handoff only applies when the URL matches, the stored token is still the one the preflight validated, and the provider builds its own client. The body is parsed with better-auth's `parseJSON`, the same parser `getSession()` uses, so dates are revived the same way. A stale token leaves nothing in the slot. Sign-in, sign-out, organisation switch, rotation and `refreshSession` all read from the server as before.

**Runtime config** (`apps/console/index.html`, `packages/app-shell/src/runtime-config.ts`). The early-branding script used to publish its request to the in-flight registry and drop it on settle. It now keeps its parsed-body promise for the page's lifetime in a slot (`Symbol.for('objectui.earlyRuntimeConfig')`, with the URL it asked). The first `initRuntimeConfig()` call takes it when the URL matches: it joins the request if it is still in flight and reads the body if it has settled. If the early fetch failed, `initRuntimeConfig()` fetches as before. Every later call re-fetches, so the repeat-call contract is unchanged.

## Before and after: one console open, live

hotcrm `objectstack dev --fresh` backend, console via Vite dev, Chromium through Playwright. The browser signs in once (cookie plus Bearer in localStorage), opens the console once to warm Vite, then the measured open is recorded. Two runs on each side gave identical counts.

| request | main 6e4f144 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| GET /api/v1/auth/get-session | 3 | 1 |
| GET /api/v1/runtime/config | 2 | 1 |
| GET /api/v1/cloud/environment-entitlements | 0 (cloud-only route, see below) | 0 |
| all /api requests of the open | 30 | 28 |
| all requests of the open (Vite dev module graph included) | 3375 | 3373 |

- get-session reads 3 on main in dev because React StrictMode replays `AuthProvider`'s mount effect. A production build shows the card's 2. With this branch it is 1 in dev too, because the replay reuses the handed-off answer.
- The entitlements route belongs to the cloud control plane, and the local backend does not mount the cloud widgets. Its count comes from the test below instead: the three plan cards, the onboarding step and the timezone notice mounted together issue 1 GET. With the shared resource ablated they issue 5.
- These numbers were measured on head 745e4b2. The later head cef7052 changes only a type annotation in `packages/auth`.

The CONTROL that the console still renders: console home after the change, light, https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/blob/73c020afbaf65fed269ff19dc5b52e169450db4f/docs/design/findings/12808/console-home-after-12808.png?raw=true (on the evidence branch `claude/issue-12808-evidence`, which is not merged here).

## Tests: one per resource, counting the requests a mount issues

- `useEnvironmentEntitlements.oneRequest-12808.test.tsx` (app-shell): five readers mounted together issue one GET. CONTROLs: an organisation change issues exactly one more; a `refreshKey` change re-resolves once for every reader; a later mount after all readers unmounted asks again.
- `sessionBootDedup.test.tsx` (console): the real preflight plus the real `AuthProvider` in StrictMode issue one get-session, and dates are revived. CONTROLs: sign-out then sign-in then `refreshSession` reads the session again; a second provider asks the server, so the answer is used once; a stale token hands nothing on.
- `runtimeConfigBootDedup.test.ts` (console, runs the shipped script text): new pin that the early answer is read even after it settled. CONTROLs: a failed early fetch still lets app-shell fetch once; a failure on both keeps the defaults. The old pin, which expected an early failure to suppress app-shell's fetch, is replaced as the card's ruling asks.

Ablation, one per new pin. Each mutation landed (`ablation-replace.mjs` anchor 1 to 0), turned the pin red, and was restored with blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty:
- entitlements: always start a resolution in `acquire` gives 5 GETs instead of 1; all 4 tests red.
- session: remove the boot-answer early return in `AuthProvider`'s mount effect gives 3 get-session instead of 1; 2 tests red.
- runtime config: never take the early answer gives 2 fetches instead of 1; 6 tests red.

## Evidence, pinned to cef7052

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell test`: exit 0. 1510 files passed and 1 skipped (1511); 14117 tests passed and 9 skipped. Run on 745e4b2; cef7052 does not touch app-shell.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/auth test`: exit 0, 33 files, 311 tests (on cef7052).
- Targeted on cef7052: the three pin files, `faviconAfterNavigation.test.tsx` and `anonSeedScope-5746.enumeration.test.tsx`, 5 files, 40 tests, exit 0.
- `type-check` for auth, app-shell and console: exit 0. `build` of the console's dependency closure (includes app-shell and auth): exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build`: exit 0.
- eslint on the touched files: exit 0 (0 errors). `pnpm check:i18n-keys` 0, `pnpm check:i18n-drift` 0, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0, `pnpm check:eager-closure` 0 (within budget), `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0 (no new citations).

## Deviations

- Session handoff: I used a module-level slot, not a new `AuthProviderProps` member. `AuthProvider` is mounted in `apps/console/src/App.tsx`, which is outside the claimed file surface. The slot mirrors the `index.html` to `runtime-config.ts` handoff, so both handoffs work the same way. `takePreflightSession` is exported from the `createAuthClient.ts` module but not from the package entry: the package's only export is `.`, whose `index.ts` names `createAuthClient` and `TokenStorage`. So `@object-ui/auth`'s published surface gains no member.
- Entitlements: the settled answer is held while readers are mounted, not for the whole page. Holding it for the page would serve a stale `hasProductionEnv` after an environment is deleted outside the list, for example from a record page, and the list then remounts at `refreshKey` 0. The card's no-stale rule forbids that.
- `CloudOnboardingNext`: on a failed summary it now waits for the shared resource's row fallback before showing `unknown`. This only happens on the failure path. The Welcome page's timezone notice already issued that rows read.
- `apps/console/src/main.tsx` is in the claimed surface but needed no change.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope and unchanged: objectui#12809 (the splash's request waves) remains open and lands after this; the server-side query counts and the cloud pricing page's metadata are not touched.
